review.assessment: This change replaces the incorrect infinity output with a proper zero-divisor guard: it checks for `$b -eq 0`, prints an error to stderr and exits non-zero on failure, and moves normal arithmetic division outside the conditional so it only executes when safe. Normal cases like `bash solution.sh 10 2` print `5` and exit cleanly; zero cases suppress stdout and terminate with a non-zero status as required. I found no defects.
